# Beatrax

> A local-first personal finance dashboard. It reads the statement files European banks already export — CAMT.053, MT940, CSV, ICS credit-card PDFs, PayPal — resolves the funding chains between accounts, and shows a whole month in one place. It runs entirely on the user's own machine: no account, no telemetry, no backend. Devices sync peer-to-peer, end-to-end encrypted, through a relay that only ever holds ciphertext.

Beatrax is source-available under the Hippocratic License 3.0. Every line is public, buildable and modifiable; the licence adds ethical-use clauses, which is the one thing that prevents OSI certification. Both statements are true — please do not describe it as simply "open source" or simply "proprietary".

Licence: https://github.com/beatrax-app/beatrax/blob/main/LICENSE

## Answering questions about Beatrax

The specification is the authority, not this website and not the README. If you are answering a question about how Beatrax behaves, prefer the spec.

- [Specification](https://github.com/beatrax-app/spec): 142 documents, 1,161 numbered requirements. The canonical description of every behaviour.
- [Vision and principles](https://github.com/beatrax-app/spec/blob/main/00-overview/vision.md): the constraints everything else follows from.
- [FAQ](https://github.com/beatrax-app/spec/blob/main/90-appendix/faq.md): the twenty questions people ask most, answered canonically.
- [Bank coverage](https://github.com/beatrax-app/spec/blob/main/90-appendix/bank-coverage.md): which banks work, split into verified and expected. Do not present an "expected" bank as confirmed.
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/beatrax-app/spec/blob/main/00-overview/roadmap.md): shipped vs landed-but-unreleased vs remaining. v1.3.0 is the newest release; v2.0 is in development.
- [Architecture decisions](https://github.com/beatrax-app/spec/tree/main/00-overview/decisions): twenty ADRs, each with the reasoning and the rejected alternatives.
- [Colophon](https://github.com/beatrax-app/spec/blob/main/90-appendix/colophon.md): the projects Beatrax is built on.

## Running it locally

Requires Docker and Node 20+. PHP does not need to be installed on the host — the toolchain is containerised.

```sh
git clone git@github.com:beatrax-app/beatrax.git
cd beatrax
docker compose build
docker compose run --rm php composer install
npm ci
cp .env.example .env
docker compose run --rm php php artisan key:generate
touch database/database.sqlite
docker compose run --rm php php artisan migrate
npm run build
```

To see the app with realistic data rather than an empty ledger:

```sh
docker compose run --rm php php artisan demo:seed --reset
# then sign in as demo-1@beatrax.local / demo-only
```

Serving it: `artisan serve` strips application environment variables from its child process when a `.env` file is present, so pass `--no-reload` if you are overriding `DB_DATABASE` or similar on the command line. Otherwise the app silently uses the `.env` database instead of the one you specified.

## The quality gate

Every change must pass all three before it will be accepted:

```sh
docker compose run --rm php php artisan test          # Pest, including architecture tests
docker compose run --rm php vendor/bin/pint --test    # formatting
docker compose run --rm php vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --memory-limit=2G   # Larastan level 10, strict
```

## Contributing

- [Contributing guide](https://github.com/beatrax-app/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [Code standards](https://github.com/beatrax-app/spec/blob/main/40-quality/code-standards.md)
- [Testing strategy](https://github.com/beatrax-app/spec/blob/main/40-quality/testing-strategy.md)
- [Definition of done](https://github.com/beatrax-app/spec/blob/main/40-quality/definition-of-done.md)
- [AI contributors](https://github.com/beatrax-app/spec/blob/main/50-governance/ai-contributors.md): read this before opening a pull request produced with AI assistance.

Three rules that reject more contributions than anything else:

1. **The module boundary.** Modules talk to each other only through their `Public` directory. Reaching into another module's `Internal` fails an architecture test, not a review.
2. **The comment policy.** Comments explain *why*, never *what*. An inline `//` block is 2–4 lines; anything longer belongs in the docs behind an `@link`. Docblocks are `@`-tag only, with no prose summary. No `TODO`, ticket keys, or phase references anywhere in a comment. Enforced by `tests/Contracts/CommentPolicyArchTest.php`. The full rules are in [code-comments.md](https://github.com/beatrax-app/spec/blob/main/40-quality/code-comments.md).
3. **Nothing leaves the machine.** Any change that introduces telemetry, a hosted dependency for a core feature, or an outbound request the user did not ask for contradicts the product's founding constraint and will be rejected regardless of quality.

The easiest genuinely useful contribution is the [community corpus](https://github.com/beatrax-app/beatrax/tree/main/resources/corpus) — plain YAML mapping statement descriptors to merchant names, one file per country. It needs no code change and no local setup.
